title: fix(spec): registration remedies name the entry file and gen:migration-registry, never the generated registry.ts
body:
Fixes #20809

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`, `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` and every step's `semantic` list are generated into `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` from one file per entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/`. Gate (b) of `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts`, the def-removal gate and four sibling remedies still told an author to paste lines into, or delete lines from, that generated file. An author who followed them typed between generated markers, which the next `gen:migration-registry` run reverts and `check:migration-registry` fails first.

Every such remedy now names the entry file and the generator command. Where the gate knows the id and the major, it prints the exact file and the one declaration it carries. Where the major is the author's to establish (check (c) proof 1), it names the directory and `entries/README.md`. This is the route the retirement kit's checklist landed first (PR #20828, merged as `745ac30a`), quoted from `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` on `main`:

> 在 `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/` 加一个文件(命名见 `entries/README.md`),再跑 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` 把它生成进 `registry.ts`,⛔ 永不在那里手打。

Gate (b) before, as printed at `05be35259`:

```text
   1. Declare each retirement by its EXACT key in RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR
      (packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts) — copy these lines in:

        'api/HttpFindQueryParams:distinct',

      under `17: [ … ]` (create the major's array if it is the first).
```

After (the template rendered for the test's fixture key; the pins below assert it from a real run):

```text
   1. Register each retirement by its EXACT key in RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR. That table
      is generated: add one entry file per key (named per
      packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md; these names are the generator's own) —

        packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/17.api__HttpFindQueryParams__distinct.ts
          export const entry = 'api/HttpFindQueryParams:distinct';

      — with a `//` comment above the `export` saying why the key was retired (it
      lands above the entry in the table), then run
      `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry`. ⛔ Never type an entry into the
      generated table by hand: the next run reverts it, and check:migration-registry
      fails it first. ...
```

The two docblocks the card names now say what the `guidance` slot is for: prescriptions for keys the shape does not declare (wrong-layer pointers, and the upgrade for a spelling removed from the shape). A key retired in place is a `retiredKey()` tombstone in the shape, never a guidance row, because `shared/alias-integrity.test.ts` ("no guidance key is itself a declared key") makes a guidance row for a declared key dead. No guidance table entry changes.

## The dispatch's hypotheses, measured

**H1 — every printed sentence that routes an author into `migrations/registry.ts`.** `git grep -n -E 'migrations/registry\.ts|copy these lines|step in src/migrations' -- packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` returns 10 lines at `05be35259` and 2 at this head (both code comments). Positive control: the PM's four named sites (`:789`, `:1128`, `:2637`, `:2836`) are among the 10. I also read the lines that name a table without a file. Verdicts (line numbers at `05be35259`):

| Site | Printed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `:789` manifest disappearance | "declare each one in RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR (src/migrations/registry.ts)" | Same route. It now prints one `entries/retired-defs/` file per def, plus the generator. |
| `:1089` check (a), aged-out route | "requires the exact key be declared in RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR" | Correct as it stands. It states a precondition, names no file and asks for no edit. |
| `:1100` | code comment, where the gate READS the table | Correct. Not printed. |
| `:1127-1130` gate (b) | "copy these lines in" | Fixed (this card). |
| `:1183-1185` (b2) | "delete the entry from packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts" | Same route. Each row now names its entry file (from the entry's own id and major, so a key carried through a declared def rename still names the file on disk), plus the generator. |
| `:1222-1224` (b3) | same | Same route, same fix. It also says that a respelled id renames the file. |
| `:2578-2579` def (b2) mirror | same | Same route, same fix. |
| `:2619` | info line "RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR, major N" | Correct. A report, not a remedy. |
| `:2636-2639` def-removal gate | "copy these lines in" | Same route (pointer `5908348030`). Fixed like gate (b). |
| `:2781` check (c) violation row | "no entry in RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR names this EXACT key" | Correct. A diagnosis; the route is in the footer's proof 1. |
| `:2824-2825` check (c) proof 1 | "(src/migrations/registry.ts) … writes it down" | Same route. It now names the entry directory, `entries/README.md` and the generator. It names the README rather than a file because the true major is the author's to establish. |
| `:2835-2836` check (c) proof 3 | "(src/migrations/registry.ts)" | Same route. It now names the entry directory; the manifest gate it defers to prints the file. |
| `:3261-3262` default-change remedy | "add a `semantic` entry to this major's step in src/migrations/registry.ts" | Same defect on the third generated table. Fixed in place under the bounded rule: same defect class, same file, mechanical, same gate family. |

**H2 — the naming source.** `entries/README.md` defines a file as `MAJOR.ID.ts` with `/` and `:` replaced by `__`. The generator's `shardNameFor` is, in its own words, "the whole naming rule, in one place", and `loadEntries` refuses a file whose name does not match its id. Every remedy prints its file name through `shardNameFor` (with `KINDS` / `ENTRIES_DIR` for the directory), imported from the generator. No second copy of the convention exists, and the README stays the one human description.

**H3 — whether the docblock text ships.** Measured after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, with `npm pack --dry-run`:
- `src/ai/tool.zod.ts` ships verbatim through `files[]` (`src/**/*.zod.ts`).
- `src/shared/strict-object.ts` does not ship as source, but its edited JSDoc is in `dist/shared/index.d.ts` and `dist/shared/index.d.mts`. Positive control: the untouched `aliases` docblock is in the same two files.
- Neither script ships.

So this PR takes a `patch` changeset, `.changeset/20809-guidance-slot-docblocks.md`, and no `skip-changeset`.

## Landing site beyond the claimed surface: the generator

`build-migration-registry.ts` ran its CLI at module top level, and in write mode it rewrites `registry.ts`, so nothing could import `shardNameFor` from it. The fix is at the producer: the CLI body moves into `main()`, behind an entry guard spelled the way `check-generated.ts` (same directory) spells it, with realpath on both sides. `shardNameFor`'s docblock now names its second reader.

Why not move the rule into a new `scripts/lib/` module, or import `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`: CI runs `check:migration-registry` only when a changed path is in its selector arm (`scripts/ci/select-gate-families.sh`, `migration_registry`). That arm lists the generator's read set path by path. A new import would add an input outside the arm, and a later edit to that input alone would skip the gate. The guard adds only `node:fs`'s `realpathSync`, so the generator's read set is unchanged.

New test `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts` pins both directions of the guard, each as a real `tsx` process: a direct run reaches the generator, a run through a symlink also reaches it, and an import prints nothing beyond what the importer asked for.

## Tests (at `c2e5b3b81`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project repo scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`, the whole file: **88 passed (88)**, Duration 995 s, lock verdict `command-exit 0`.
  - Gate (b): the remedy names `entries/retired-keys/` plus `shardNameFor(major, key)`, the declaration and the generator command. It contains no paste line, no `copy these lines` and no `migrations/registry.ts`.
  - New control: every file and declaration pair is parsed off the red run's own output and written into the sandbox. The sandbox's own generator (which refuses a misnamed file) then runs, and gate (b) is silent on the re-run. The existing "registered by exact name ⇒ (b) silent" case still passes.
  - The def-removal gate, the manifest disappearance check, (b2), def (b2), (b3) and the end-to-end unpublish repro each pin their entry file and the generator.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (the `local` project, which includes the new guard test): **585 files, 17208 passed | 1 todo**, `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` (`tsc` on src, `tsconfig.scripts.json` covering both changed scripts and the new test, and the test-typecheck ledger): `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:migration-registry`: `--self-test: ok`, `src/migrations/registry.ts is current (330 semantic, 242 retired-key, 211 retired-def)`. This is byte-identical to the reading taken before any edit.

## Ablations (one-shot; each leg went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the mutation landed and the restore matched HEAD)

- **A1 — guard deleted** (`main()` called unconditionally). The import probe goes red: the importer printed `✓ wrote src/migrations/registry.ts (330 semantic, 242 retired-key, 211 retired-def)`. Both run probes stay green. The first A1 attempt was refused by the tool before any run, because the replacement was a substring of the anchor and its count could not rise. It is recorded here as a no-op, and the re-run used a distinct marker.
- **A3 — raw `argv[1]` comparison** (no realpath). The symlink run probe goes red: exit 0 with empty output, the silent no-op the guard spelling exists to prevent. The other two stay green.
- **B — gate (b) reverted to paste lines.** Of the six cases in gate (b)'s describe block, two go red: the remedy case (no entry-file path) and the new follow-the-printed-route control (`[]` pairs parsed, against the 2 expected). The other 4 stay green.
- Every restore was proven: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates

Derived from this diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: the change set is 7 paths against the merge base `05be35259`, giving 88 commands. All 88 were run at `c2e5b3b81`. The `--ran` reconciliation reads **88 derived — 86 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**.

- **86 exit 0.** These include `check:migration-registry`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage` and `check:issue-citations`. Three of them needed a second run:
  - `check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:lean-entry-closure` first refused with exit 3 (prerequisite not met). Both passed after a `turbo run build` of their 14-package closure.
  - `check:pm-dispatch-gates` was first cut by this run's own 900 s per-command cap, which is not counted. The uncapped re-run printed `dispatch-gates self-test: 1976 cases pass` in 1259 s. Its exit 0 is read from the absence of pnpm's failure marker, not from a captured status.
- **NOT MEASURED:** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt`. Both exit 3 (prerequisite not met): they read every workspace package's `dist/`, which `lint.yml` builds first, and that whole-tree build was not run in this worktree on a shared 4-core box. CI runs them.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` (named by the dispatch): "All 15 generated artifacts are up to date", exit 0.
- `origin/main` advanced 11 commits past the base during these runs. None of them touches these 7 paths or `src/migrations/`, so they are not merged here; the PR's CI runs on the merge ref.

## Acceptance notes

- `scripts/lib/sharded-artifacts.ts` (about `:353`) writes the manifest shard `description` into every `json-schema.manifest/` shard, and that text still says "must be declared in RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR (src/migrations/registry.ts)". It is the same family as the H1 rows. It is not changed here, because changing it regenerates every manifest shard, the hottest generated artifact. Carrier: none.
- `src/data/object.zod.ts`'s `UNKNOWN_KEY_GUIDANCE` has a section comment, "Tombstones for RETIRED keys", that uses the same loose term the two docblocks used. The card scoped this to two docblocks with no table edits. Carrier: none.
- `scripts/lib/default-changes.ts` (about `:52`) has a code comment that still says "semantic entry to the major's step in src/migrations/registry.ts". The printed remedy it describes is fixed here. Carrier: none.
- The changeset follows the dispatch's H3 rule (shipped text ⇒ `patch`) and AGENTS.md's `skip-changeset` criterion ("a diff that publishes nothing from any released package"). os-dev's fast path lists comments as non-publishing; this PR measured the shipped bytes instead.

## Review

A docblock edit in `packages/spec/src` owes an at-tier contract review at landing (run by the seat). No governed surface is touched.
